title: Anthropic targets upto $1.4T valuation with $70 to $78 IPO price range
summary: Anthropic targets upto $1.4T valuation with $70 to $78 IPO price range
detailed: Anthropic set an IPO price band of $70 to $78 per share, potentially valuing the company between $1.26 trillion and $1.41 trillion.
Major technology companies including Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, and Broadcom will purchase $26 billion in shares through a private placement.
The company has raised a total of $130 billion in funding and was previously valued at $965 billion.
Anthropic reported revenue rising from $41 million in 2023 to $4.5 billion in 2025, alongside first-half 2025 revenue of $1.16 billion and losses of $12.96 billion.
sentences: AI company Anthropic has set $70 to $78 as the price band for its initial public offering (IPO) which potentially values the company in the range of $1.26 trillion to $1.41 trillion.
The company will be offering 825 million shares.
According to the filings, leading technology companies such as Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom will be purchasing $26 billion worth of shares in Anthropic through a private placement.
Reports suggest that the company could raise in excess of $100 billion.
The report also said Anthropic will be pricing the shares of its IPO on November 18 and trade on November 19.
The shares will be traded on Nasdaq stock exchange.
Anthropic, which has raised a total of $130 billion in funding, was last valued at $965 billion.
The AI company's valuation comes at a time when investors are questioning the valuation of AI companies.
Anthropic, which was founded by Dario Amodei and others in 2021, was earlier seeking a valuation of $2 trillion.
In comparison, the company reported revenue of $1.16 billion and losses of $12.96 billion in the first half of 2025.
Anthropic’s growth has been remarkable, with revenue rising from just $41 million in 2023 to $4.5 billion in 2025.
In its IPO filing, Anthropic said, “We believe that AI is one of the most consequential technologies in human history.

It further noted that the world has only begun to use the capabilities of today’s frontier models, and the gap between what Claude can do and how broadly it is used represents one of our largest growth opportunities, alongside continued advances at the frontier.
